R1's 'Abstract 형태로 제공되었다' line is filler, but R2's errors empty out its performance-analysis section.

R2 has more unsupported claims: it attributes E10's satisfaction and re-participation indicators to E2's meta-analysis twice, says E5 'confirmed' program effects twice without support, and cites E18 for the small-group proposal that comes from E2. R1's section 4 is weaker but stays closer to the evidence, which outweighs R2's more accurate attributions in a few other places (E3, 성지은·김수진) and R1's 'Abstract 형태' filler sentence.

R2 is narrowly better. R1 gets two findings backwards. It says the number of studies is growing (E3 says they are scarce). It also presents the null results of 성지은·김수진, a single study that E2 cites, as E2's own meta-analysis result, even though E2 found an overall effect size of 0.624. R1 also leaves a stray meta-sentence about E5 being 'Abstract 형태로 제공'. R2 has its own serious faults: in section 4 it attributes E10's satisfaction and re-participation metrics to E2, and twice states 'E5 confirmed effects' without support. Outside section 4, R2 attributes findings correctly and is more specific (E6 중간 수준 상관, E7 지식·기술·태도, E11 gap).

R2 also invents E6 results (dependence rising with age, effects of SNS and game time), recasts E7 as a buffering effect and attributes E10's text to E13. R1's slips are mostly misattributions (E16's method placed under E17, E5's content-frequency point given to E6 and E3), so R1 is somewhat more faithful even though R2 is cleaner in places, such as section 3's citations, E14 in section 4 and E2's 'inner strength' point in section 6.
